description:
THIS IS A DESIGN AND LICENSING FAULT, NOT A MISCONFIGURATION. Do not treat it as an env var someone forgot to set.
VERIFIED VERBATIM IN SOURCE by R81 at ct/src/lib/ai/adapter.ts:78-82, the second refusal branch logs: "Anthropic's Claude Code policy permits OAuth/subscription auth for ordinary individual use only -- never to serve a request on behalf of a different person. Set AI_PROVIDER=openrouter before this product serves anyone other than that one account."
THE TENSION THAT MATTERS: the owner ruled on 2026-09-08 that the END-USER DEFAULT for L1/L2/L3 is Claude Code Sonnet High. A Claude Code SUBSCRIPTION / OAuth credential cannot lawfully serve end users' requests. So serving customers on that path is not one config change away -- it is not permitted, and the guard fails closed precisely to prevent it. adapter.ts:56-58's own comment shows the fail-closed behaviour was deliberate and correct.
MECHANICS, verified line by line and CORRECTING an earlier reading of my own: `if (!allowed)` at adapter.ts:68 fires BEFORE `if (userId !== allowed)` at :78, so with RAJAT_USER_ID unset the code refuses for LITERALLY EVERYONE, the owner included -- not merely for non-owners as first recorded. And resolveProviderName() at :87 is `process.env.AI_PROVIDER ?? "claude-cli"`, so an UNSET variable does not disable the guard, it SELECTS the guarded provider. .env.example declares NEITHER variable (grep -c returns 0 for both), so any environment provisioned from it lands on the refusing branch by default.
BOTH BRANCHES: (A) unset or claude-cli -> L1 refuses for 100% of users and modelCalls reads 0 IDENTICALLY to a genuine "the software resolved everything" result. (B) openrouter -> adapter.ts:65 returns immediately, RAJAT_USER_ID is never read, the guard restricts nobody. One environment string is the entire difference between "no one gets AI" and "everyone gets AI".
OWNER DECISION REQUIRED -- money and licensing, explicitly outside this session's authority. Two lawful routes preserve the intent: end users on OpenRouter, or end users on an Anthropic API KEY (API-key auth is legitimate for serving others and would keep "Sonnet High" as the end-user default in substance). NEITHER IS BEING CHOSEN HERE and AI_PROVIDER has NOT been set by either session.
A CONNECTION NEITHER SESSION HAD MADE: adapter.ts:51-53 records that RAJAT_USER_ID identifies democeo@projexa-ai.com -- the SAME demo admin account whose plaintext credential R81 D1-01 found inside a recovered Google Drive foundational document (see R81_F04). So the single identity the entire AI guard is keyed to is an account with a known-leaked, unrotated password on a public domain. Rotating it is an owner action AND it would change the value this guard depends on.
Independently verified by both concurrently running sessions, each reading the source rather than accepting the other's report.

[R81 D8-01 ADDENDUM] An exhaustive repo-wide search settles the provisioning question: RAJAT_USER_ID appears in exactly 10 files (.env.local, one commit message, 3 registers, 5 source/test files) and NEITHER variable is set by any .env.production or by vercel.json in EITHER repository. So nothing checked in would move a deployment off the refusing branch -- a fresh environment provisioned from the repo lands on Branch A by construction, not by oversight. The live Production values themselves remain CANNOT-ESTABLISH from code and were measured separately by listing variable NAMES only.
justification: Reclassified from High to Critical and from a configuration fault to a design/licensing fault. A misconfiguration is fixed by setting a variable; this cannot be, because the ruled-for default is not a lawful way to serve end users. Filing it as a config gap would have led someone to "fix" it by setting AI_PROVIDER=claude-cli in Production, which is the one action the code exists to prevent.

description: The receivedQuantity increment is NOT idempotent and there is NO over-receipt cap. Two receipts posted against the same purchase-order line add twice, so erp_purchase_order_items.receivedQuantity can exceed quantity and the header rollup will read the order as completed on the strength of an over-receipt. Pre-existing and PRE-DISCLOSED by the R80 session when it handed over the D6-07 verification, rather than discovered afterwards -- filed here so it is not mistaken for something the end-to-end test missed. getThreeWayMatchReport already surfaces the condition as over_received, so it is visible downstream but not prevented at the point of write. NOT fixed by R81: a cap is a business rule (is over-receipt forbidden, tolerated within a percentage, or allowed with a flag?) and that is a product decision, not a defect to patch unilaterally.
justification: A quantity that can silently exceed what was ordered is a data-integrity issue, but the remedy needs a stated tolerance policy. Recorded with its downstream detection so the next person sees both the hole and the existing net.

description: THERE ARE ZERO USABLE EMBEDDINGS, SO NO VECTOR TIER CAN EVER MATCH. Measured live: compliance.embeddings holds 981 rows across exactly TWO model values -- hash-pseudo-vector (838 rows, not a real model) and unknown-legacy (143 rows), and ALL 143 unknown-legacy rows are quarantined=true. So usable, real, un-quarantined embeddings = 0. The retrieval query filters on `AND e.embedding_model = ${model}`, and since neither stored string is a real provider model id, that predicate can never match a live model. Any semantic/vector tier built on this reads an empty set by construction. Compounding it: compliance.memory_records, memory_versions and memory_sources are all 0 rows -- nothing has ever been ingested -- and 0 of 278 organisations hold the institutional_memory entitlement that gates both the read and the write path. A prior register row citing "143" is citing 143 QUARANTINED rows.
justification: IMG cannot be described as working, or even as measurable, while its vector substrate is structurally unmatchable and its content tables are empty. Reporting a proven-point count without this denominator would overstate it badly.

description: THE APPEND-ONLY GUARDS BIND ONE ROLE ONLY, AND ONE TABLE HAS NO UPDATE GUARD AT ALL. Read from pg_catalog: every integrity guard except graph_edge_guard fires only when current_user = 'app_runtime'. service_role and postgres hold full DML on all five tables PLUS USING true bypass policies, so the audit trail that memory_versions exists to be is not protected from the roles most likely to be used by a script or an MCP session. Separately, platform.graph_edge has NO UPDATE-immutability guard -- there is no immutability branch anywhere in graph_edge_guard's body -- so a graph edge can be rewritten in place. IMG-036 cannot detect this because its proof tests only for the presence of a BEFORE DELETE trigger, so the register will keep reporting that guard as present while UPDATE stays open. NOT PROVEN BY WRITE: the audit had SELECT-only access, so that the triggers actually RAISE was read from definitions and tgenabled='O', not demonstrated. Proving them needs a write attempt inside a rolled-back transaction, which requires a verified backup first per Addendum B GG-05.
justification: An append-only guarantee that only holds for one of three roles is not an append-only guarantee, and a register proof that tests for the wrong trigger event will never reveal it. Both halves have to be recorded or the next audit repeats this one.

description: THE IMG REGISTER CONTRADICTS ITSELF AND ITS PROOFS ARE PARTLY UNRUNNABLE. Measured live: 74 rows; only 37 carry a closure_proof_sql at all; only 30 have EVER been run, all inside one window on 2026-09-04 04:03-08:36 UTC; 21 stored true. The other 37 rows carry NO proof mechanism and sit at result_bool=false, which is a DEFAULT, not a finding -- they are unmeasurable, and a register that reports them as false is reporting a value it never computed. WORSE, A STORED FALSE POSITIVE WAS FOUND AND CONFIRMED BY RUNNING THE ROW'S OWN PROOF: IMG-016 was stored TRUE while its proof returns 0 against an expected ">= 1". Corrected to FALSE by R81. Its proof also can NEVER pass -- it searches information_schema.routines for a compliance routine named like %recall%, but the recall ladder is TypeScript, not SQL, so the proof tests the wrong artefact entirely. An independent re-run of all 37 proof-bearing rows disagreed with the register on 8 of 37. THE HONEST POSITION MUST ALWAYS BE STATED WITH BOTH FIGURES: 26 of 37 executed proofs true, AND 37 of 74 never measured. A single number is not reportable here.
justification: A register whose rows can be true while their own proofs fail is worse than no register, because it is quoted as evidence. This is the same class as the closure-gate hole that let six requirements close on a CI-red test.

description: WHETHER THE AI DID THE WORK IS NOT RECOVERABLE FROM THE DATABASE. `executor: "software"` is HARDCODED at run-submission.ts:1020 -- verified directly by R81, not taken from a report. The 'ai' enum value is never assigned anywhere, and pipeline_tasks carries no source or level column. So for any executed business-data write, the record cannot say whether a human, the software tiers, or a model produced it. THIS IS THE ATTRIBUTION REQUIREMENT FAILING AT ITS ROOT: three further fields have no write site at all -- the MODEL ID is resolved at openrouter.ts:59 and discarded at :78-84 (and can change between requests via a 60s-TTL hot-reload row, so even the model that answered is unknowable); the PROMPT HASH is never computed and is explicitly declined at run-submission.ts:300-304; and the RETRIEVED ITEM IDS (the BOQ candidate set sent at level1.ts:102-106) are never returned or written and become unreconstructable once a new BOQ version exists. COMPOUNDING IT: because L1 refuses when RAJAT_USER_ID is unset, modelCalls reads 0 -- IDENTICALLY to a genuine "the software resolved everything" result. A metric that reads the same whether the AI worked perfectly or was switched off cannot measure the 95/5 split the programme is built on.
justification: An ERP that cannot say whether a model touched a financial write has no AI audit trail, and the one metric meant to prove the software-first design reads identically in the success and the switched-off case. Both halves have to be fixed together or the measurement stays meaningless.

description:
THE CONNECTOR SCOPE GATE IS BUILT, TESTED, AND NOT ON THE PRODUCTION PATH. Verified directly by R81, not accepted from a report. ct/src/lib/services/connector-scope-gate-service.ts implements executeGatedConnectorAction, which enforces GOOGLE_CONNECTOR_SCOPE_ALLOW_LIST (composio-connectors.ts:214-235, gmail/googledrive/googlesheets/googledocs mapped to read/edit/write), fails closed for any unlisted toolkit (no_allow_list_recorded), and unconditionally refuses KNOWN_DELETE_CAPABLE_SCOPES. It has a full test suite. IT HAS ZERO PRODUCTION CALL SITES: a search across src finds executeGatedConnectorAction ONLY inside connector-scope-gate-service.test.ts, and getAuthConfigScopes ONLY in its own definition (composio-connectors.ts:367) plus tests. Meanwhile the LIVE read paths import executeAction directly (connector-data-service.ts:38) and call it at :117 (GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS) and :211 (GOOGLEDRIVE_FIND_FILE), bypassing the gate entirely. So a user's Gmail and Drive can be read through a path that never consults the allow-list, never applies the delete-capable-scope refusal, and never writes the audit record the gate produces. WHAT MAKES THIS WORSE THAN AN UNBUILT CONTROL: the gate's passing tests are a source of FALSE ASSURANCE -- an auditor reading them concludes the control is enforced. LATENT, NOT ACTIVE, and that distinction is recorded honestly: COMPOSIO_API_KEY is unprovisioned (CRR-007, a standing declined purchase, disclosed at composio-connectors.ts:190-196), so no connector call has run live. The exposure begins the moment that key is provisioned. ALSO MISSING, verified by an exhaustive search returning nothing: the PER-USER CONSENT RECORD the owner ruling requires -- no consent_/granted_scopes/scope_grant table or column exists anywhere; connector_accounts stores only status and connectedEmail, so the gate would be evaluated against shared app-level auth_config scopes rather than what any individual user actually granted.

The defect is confirmed exactly as filed: executeGatedConnectorAction (connector-scope-gate-service.ts:109)

description:
POSTING A GOODS RECEIPT FAILS WITH A 500 WHENEVER A LINE ACTUALLY NAMES A STOCK ITEM. Found by driving the real UI end to end, and confirmed three independent ways.
 (1) HTTP: "Post to Stock" returned 500, surfaced to PROJEXA as {"error":"Failed to submit goods receipt","code":"UPSTREAM_500"}.
 (2) SERVER LOG, verbatim: "v1 projexa procurement goods-receipt submit error: Error: nested withTenantContext: a transaction for org 4ecc472f-4152-4310-ae8d-cf8b7c52ab6d (opened 2026-09-08T14:13:45.202Z) is still open, and org ... tried to open a second one. Pass the open transaction's db handle down instead -- one request must never hold two of the five app_runtime connections (src/lib/db/tenant-scoped.ts)."
 (3) DATABASE STATE, which is the damning part: purchase order klpg9hy8ioodfgwc2blxqyni, item_id NOT NULL, sits at status=draft with received_quantity=0, its receipt stranded at status=draft, and ZERO erp_stock_ledger_entries rows. Nothing was credited, nothing was posted, and the order cannot progress.
CONTRAST, same session, same servers, same flow: a FREE-TEXT line (item_id NULL) reached status=completed with received 5 of 5 and correctly zero stock rows. So the failure is specific to the stock-item path.
MECHANISM: submitPurchaseReceipt already holds a withTenantContext transaction; recordStockReceipt opens a SECOND one for the same org. tenant-scoped.ts's guard detects the nesting and throws. The free-text path never reaches it, because `if (!item.itemId) continue` short-circuits first.
WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW, and it matters: before ct 754cef17 and projexa 19491a5, PROJEXA's PO screens never sent an itemId, so recordStockReceipt was effectively unreachable from PROJEXA. 754cef17 correctly moved the receivedQuantity credit above the guard, and 19491a5 let PO lines carry a stock item -- TOGETHER THEY MADE THIS PATH REACHABLE FOR THE FIRST TIME AND IT DOES NOT WORK. The fix is right in intent; the newly-reachable branch is broken. This is not a regression introduced by those commits, it is a latent defect they exposed.
RELATED: the guard's own message ties this to the max:5 app_runtime pool (see R81_F17 and the concurrent session's standing pool finding) -- the nesting rule exists precisely because one request must not hold two of five connections.
NOT FIXED BY R81: erp-goods-receipt-service.ts is owned by the concurrent R80 session by agreement. Reported to it directly with the log line and the PO id.

[R81 UPDATE 2026-09-08] FIX SHIPPED BY THE CONCURRENT R80 SESSION as compliance-tracker 6b56c00b, and R81 VERIFIED THE FIX IS CORRECT IN SOURCE: recordStockReceipt now takes an optional existingDb handle (erp-inventory-service.ts:73, `return existingDb ? run(existingDb) : withTenantContext(...)`) and submitPurchaseReceipt now PASSES it (erp-goods-receipt-service.ts:175-178, `await recordStockReceipt(ctx, {...}, db)`). Omitting the handle preserves the previous behaviour exactly. That session also fixed an identical twin in erp-returns-service.ts, and disclosed erp-inventory-planning-service.ts as a wider un-fixed instance rather than bundling it.
THE ORIGINAL DEFECT IS CONFIRMED GONE FROM THE LOG: no "nested withTenantContext" error has been emitted since the fix was loaded.
BUT THE END-TO-END RE-RUN IS NOT PROVEN, AND THIS ROW STAYS OPEN. Across four attempts the browser run never completed cleanly: 503 UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT twice (PROJEXA aborts an upstream call at 8s), one 404 caused by a corrupted .next build manifest that a mid-write server kill had left behind (cleared by deleting .next; the route file was present and the tree clean at the fix commit throughout), and repeated 15s locator.click timeouts. Free RAM ranged 0.04-0.71 GB with two dev servers, a second Claude session and this one on a 7.82 GB machine. NONE of those failures is attributable to the fix, and NONE of them is evidence FOR it either.
SO THE HONEST STATE IS: originally FAILED with three independent confirmations (HTTP 500, the verbatim nested-transaction log line, and database state showing draft/received 0/receipt stranded/zero ledger rows); fix reviewed and correct in source; NOT YET RE-PROVEN THROUGH THE UI. It must not be closed until a run on a machine with real headroom shows po_status advancing, received_quantity credited, AND at least one erp_stock_ledger_entries row at valuation_rate 211 rather than 0. The spec is committed-adjacent at projexa e2e/r81-d607b-stock-and-cancel.spec.ts and is deliberately left RED.

[R81 K5-01 CLOSED 2026-09-08 -- citation ct afe275c9, test src/lib/services/erp-goods-receipt-nested-transaction.test.ts]
CLOSED ON MY OWN VERIFICATION, NOT ON THE FIXING SESSION'S REPORT.
FIRST, THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS: commit 6b56c00b, which I previously recorded as "the fix, verified correct in source", DID NOT FIX THIS. Threading the open db handle into recordStockReceipt was necessary but NOT SUFFICIENT -- requireErpEnabled() opens its OWN withTenantContext (isErpEnabledForOrg -> isBranchEnabledForOrg) and runs BEFORE the existingDb branch is ever reached, so a caller already inside a transaction still tripped assertNotNested, just at a different line. My reading of the source was right about what the diff did and wrong about whether it was enough. My "stale dev-server module" explanation for the post-fix 500 was also wrong: that was a TRUE NEGATIVE. afe275c9 corrects it using isErpEnabledForOrgWithDb, the handle-accepting variant R74 Phase 10 added for exactly this shape, applied to recordStockReceipt, recordStockIssue AND getItemValuation.
MY INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION:
 1. Ran the test myself against the REAL database: 6 pass / 0 fail.
 2. Ran my OWN falsifiability cycle rather than accepting the reported one. First attempt was a NO-OP -- my patch asserted a single occurrence and the pattern appears THREE times, so the file never changed and the resulting "6 pass" proved nothing. Caught it, redid it reverting ALL THREE gates to the 6b56c00b shape: 1 pass / 5 FAIL with the verbatim production error, "submitPurchaseReceipt threw instead of completing: nested withTenantContext: a transaction for org 4ecc472f... is still open, and org 4ecc472f... tried to open a second one."
 3. Restored BYTE-IDENTICAL to HEAD (sha256 of working file == sha256 of the HEAD blob, CRLF 0): 6 pass / 0 fail again.
 4. Confirmed the test asserts THIS FAULT'S OWN RECORDED CLOSE CONDITION, verbatim and not by paraphrase: status advances past draft (expect(po?.status).not.toBe("draft"), and one of partially_received/completed); received_quantity credited on BOTH lines; and the load-bearing one -- expect(Number(entry.valuationRate)).toBe(211) with an explicit .not.toBe(0). It also asserts exactly ONE ledger row for TWO received lines, which is the free-text-versus-stock-item split that is the entire substance of the original fix.
A KNOWN LIMITATION, RECORDED SO NOBODY MISREADS CI: this test SKIPS under CI's placeholder database credentials (8 skipped, with a visible reason). It therefore does NOT pass in CI, and CI going green must never be read as evidence for this fix. That is a property of the CI environment, not of the fix. Per ruling R81-RULING-03 as sharpened -- check test OUTCOME, not job conclusion -- a skip is not a pass, and this fault is closed on the LOCAL real-database run plus the falsifiability cycle above, which is stronger evidence than a browser run could give.
WHY NOT ALSO CONFIRMED THROUGH THE BROWSER: the read-back path is itself broken (fault R81_F27 -- the single-PO route 404s on orders that exist and that the list route returns). The service-layer test is the better instrument here, exactly as the fixing session argued.
justification: A purchase receipt that names a stock item -- the ordinary case for a construction ERP buying materials -- cannot be posted at all, and fails in a way that leaves the order silently stuck in draft with no stock and no credit. It is the exact half of the procure-to-receive chain that the previous fix was believed to have completed.

description:
THE NESTING GUARD THROWS IN DEV AND TEST BUT ONLY WARNS IN PRODUCTION, AND ITS STATED RATIONALE IS CONTRADICTED BY ITS OWN LIST. Verified in source: assertNotNested() reads NODE_ENV per call and `if (env === "development" || env === "test") throw`, otherwise `console.warn(...)` and THE REQUEST CONTINUES. The documented reason is that "nesting is a latency/exhaustion bug, not a correctness one: the query results are right, they just cost too much."
THAT CLAIM IS FALSE FOR AT LEAST ONE ENTRY IN THE GUARD'S OWN KNOWN-NESTING LIST, which says of the goods-receipt site: "also a correctness problem: the stock ledger commits in a different transaction from the receipt status it is posting for". So for that path, production leniency does not degrade performance -- it splits an atomic operation. A failure between the two commits leaves stock posted against a receipt that never reached submitted. That is silent data corruption, and it is silent precisely BECAUSE production only warns.
WHAT THIS MEANS IN PRACTICE, and it is the inverse of how it looks: the HTTP 500 R81 hit in dev (fault R81_F25) was the SAFE manifestation. The same code in production would have completed the request, warned into a log nobody reads, and left the ledger and the receipt in separate transactions. The loud failure was the good outcome.
THE LIST IS A SNAPSHOT AND FIVE OF ITS SIX ENTRIES ARE STILL LIVE. Measured this block: erp-returns-service.ts now passes the open handle (fixed by the concurrent session alongside goods-receipt in ct 6b56c00b). STILL NESTING, none passing a handle: erp-inventory-planning-service.ts (recordStockReceipt / recordStockIssue / getItemValuation), erp-invoicing-service.ts and erp-payment-entries-service.ts (isPeriodOpenForDate), construction-valuation-service.ts and erp-contract-service.ts (createSalesInvoice). EVERY ONE IS A FINANCIAL OR INVENTORY PATH. The sixth, orchestra-execution-logger.ts, is fire-and-forget and its own note correctly assesses it as degrading to a skipped log line.
THE GUARD ITSELF SAYS "This list is a snapshot, not a maintained registry: the guard itself is the live answer." That is true in dev, where it throws. It is NOT true in production, where the guard answers with a warning and proceeds.
NOT FIXED HERE: these are the concurrent session's files by agreement, and the remedy per site is a judgement about transaction boundaries in money-handling code, not a mechanical edit. Filed with the mechanism so it is not rediscovered a third time -- R43_MGR_01 removed one instance in August and another was still live in September.
justification: Production converts a loud, immediately-diagnosed failure into a silent split of an atomic financial operation, on five live paths, while the guard's own comment asserts correctness is not at stake. The one case that was actually exercised proved otherwise within minutes.

description:
THE SINGLE-PURCHASE-ORDER ROUTE 404s ON ORDERS THAT EXIST AND THAT THE LIST ROUTE RETURNS TO THE SAME CALLER. Reproduced on four separate purchase orders in one authenticated session.
EVIDENCE, three independent layers:
 (1) DATABASE: all four ids exist in compliance.erp_purchase_orders with org_id 4ecc472f-4152-4310-ae8d-cf8b7c52ab6d -- two draft, two completed.
 (2) LIST ROUTE: GET /api/purchase-orders returns 200 with 55 orders and CONTAINS ALL FOUR IDS.
 (3) SINGLE ROUTE: GET /api/procurement/purchase-orders/<id> returns 404 {"error":"Not Found"} for ALL FOUR, and DELETE (which is the cancel verb) likewise 404s. PROJEXA request log: upstreamMs 88-126, so compliance-tracker answered FAST with a 404 -- not a timeout, not a cold compile.
THIS IS NOT A TENANT-ISOLATION LEAK, and that was checked before filing rather than assumed. 59 purchase orders exist across 3 orgs; exactly 55 belong to the E2E org; the list returned exactly 55. The list is CORRECTLY scoped. Also ruled out: the apparent org mismatch in the logs (PROJEXA orgId 42d7bac5-ffe1-4e10-a783-deaa90f8ce03 vs the rows' 4ecc472f-...) is NOT a mismatch -- public.veridian_credentials maps 42d7bac5 -> 4ecc472f, so they are the same tenant in two id spaces.
SO THE SINGLE-PO ROUTE IS THE BROKEN ONE. getPurchaseOrder() filters `id = ? AND orgId = ctx.orgId` inside withTenantContext, so a 404 means ctx.orgId did not resolve to 4ecc472f for that call -- while the list route, for the SAME caller in the SAME session, resolved it correctly. Two routes serving the same resource resolve the caller's organisation differently.
IT IS A REGRESSION, not a standing condition: the same route served the same ids successfully earlier today (R81 read po_status=completed, received 5 of 5, through it at ~12:50). compliance-tracker moved 5b2ef432 -> 7a13df3d -> 6b56c00b in between.
IMPACT: it BLOCKS verification, not just reading. D6-07's read-back and the cancelled-PO half both go through this route, so R81_F25 cannot be re-proven while it is broken. The failure is in the INSTRUMENT, and R81_F25 must not be judged on runs that died here.
NOT FIXED HERE: compliance-tracker service code is the concurrent session's by agreement. Handed over with the four ids, the log lines and the getPurchaseOrder() filter as the starting point.
justification: A resource that lists but cannot be opened is broken for every consumer, and it silently converts a verification failure into what looks like a product failure. Filed only after ruling out a tenant leak and an id-space mismatch, either of which would have been a materially different and worse claim.

description:
AN UNRESTRICTED read,write API KEY IS ONE ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE FROM BEING LIVE FOR EXTERNAL INTEGRATORS. projexa_demo_key (org projexa_demo_org) has scopes "read,write" (unrestricted) and rateLimitPerMinute null (unlimited). The comment names the risk: fine for its original purpose, "unsafe the moment it's handed to external integrators as the sandbox".
GUARD: KNOWN_DEMO_KEY_IDS is built from process.env.DEMO_API_KEY_IDS, which is UNSET in every environment, so the key is rejected outright today. Setting that one variable activates the path.
NOTE THE ASYMMETRY, which is the actual defect: effectiveRateLimitFor() clamps demo keys to 30/min, so the RATE ceiling is applied when the key is allowlisted -- but the SCOPE ceiling is not. An external sandbox user would get a throttled key that can still WRITE to the demo org.
DORMANT-BEHIND-A-GUARD. Recommended: clamp demo-key scopes to read-only in the same place the rate limit is clamped, so activating the env var cannot grant writes.
justification: The guard is an unset env var, the activation is a deliberate act someone will eventually take to publish a sandbox, and the code clamps the harmless dimension while leaving write access intact.

description:
A CROSS-TENANT DATA LEAK IS ONE PERFORMANCE CHANGE AWAY, AND THE CODE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN COMMENT. Next's ordinary fetch() cache keys on URL + METHOD + BODY ONLY -- NOT headers. Every PROJEXA read reaches VERIDIAN through callVeridian() -> fetchWithTimeout(), where tenancy is carried SOLELY by the per-org Bearer token from resolveApiKey(), and the URL path (e.g. "/currencies") is IDENTICAL across orgs. So adding `next: { revalidate }` to that shared fetch would serve org A's cached response to org B. The comment states it outright: "That is a real cross-tenant leak (same class as E-45), not a theoretical one."
WHAT HOLDS IT SHUT TODAY: every call site passes cache: "no-store" (lines 627, 723, 755, 817). That is the entire guard. A single perf-minded edit adding revalidate to the shared fetch removes it, and nothing tests for it.
CLASSIFICATION: DORMANT-BEHIND-A-GUARD -- a live path with a fuse, not dead code. This is precisely the class that produced R81_F25: a documented defect held shut by one condition, until a later change removed the condition.
RECOMMENDED, not done here: an assertion that fetchWithTimeout() never receives a cache mode other than no-store, so the guard is enforced rather than remembered.

--- SEVERITY CORRECTED Critical -> High, 2026-09-08, and the correction is mine to own ---
This was filed as "one line from a cross-tenant leak", which assumed Next caches fetch by default.
It does not, and has not since Next 15; projexa pins next ^16.2.10 (package.json:60) and ct 16.2.12.
So the leak is LATENT -- it requires someone to actively ADD caching (a next:{revalidate} on the
shared fetch, or removing a cache:"no-store") -- not live. An independent verification pass overturned
the original severity and it was right to.
What remains true and is why this stays High rather than closing: the safety of every proxied
per-tenant read depends on four hand-written cache:"no-store" opt-outs, the hazard is invisible at the
call site, and the triggering change reviews like an ordinary optimisation. That is now ENFORCED
rather than documented -- projexa 342c6a4 adds src/lib/veridian-client.cache-safety.test.ts, which
fails the build if any fetchWithTimeout call site loses its opt-out, if the shared fetch gains a
revalidate, or if the sanctioned cached helper stops keying on organizationId. Proven falsifiable:
removing one opt-out names that exact call site (veridian-client.ts:617).
justification: The blast radius is every proxied read route for every tenant, the trigger is an ordinary optimisation, and the only thing preventing it is a convention repeated at four call sites with nothing enforcing it.

description:
/api/me INTERMITTENTLY RETURNS HTTP 200 WITH EVERY FIELD NULL, AND ONLY ONE PAGE DEFENDS AGAINST IT. The comment records it as live-confirmed by real Playwright, 3 of 3 trials: a transient server-side session-resolution race returns 200 with id/name/email/orgId all null, and the old code rendered a permanently empty Profile with no retry. The remedy written for it, fetchMeWithSessionRetry(), is used at EXACTLY ONE call site (settings/page.tsx:154). THE SERVER-SIDE RACE ITSELF WAS NEVER FIXED.
STILL UNGUARDED, doing a bare fetch("/api/me") on mount: crm/{page,accounts,campaigns,contacts,leads,opportunities,pipeline}.tsx (setSalesEnabled), erp/{journal-entries,procurement}/page.tsx (setErpEnabled), capability-registry/page.tsx:82 (setIsAdmin), finops/page.tsx:124 (setRole), hr/attendance/page.tsx:88, hr/page.tsx:65, erp/fixed-assets/[id]/page.tsx:72, pms/page.tsx:58.
CONSEQUENCE: on a raced load those pages silently render the WRONG ENTITLEMENT STATE -- CRM and ERP modules hidden as "not enabled", admin controls hidden, role null -- with no error and no retry. A user sees a product with features missing and nothing to indicate why.
The fix is per-page (use the existing helper) but the real fix is the server-side race.
justification: A silent wrong-entitlement render is indistinguishable from "the feature was never bought", and the retry helper proving the race is real is applied to one page of fifteen.

description:
THE CHECK THAT ENFORCES "EVERY API ROUTE MUST CALL requireAuth()" WAS WRITTEN, COMMITTED, AND NEVER WIRED INTO CI. Its own comment records why: "NOT yet wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml as of this commit -- this session's git token lacks the workflow OAuth scope", and it writes out the exact remedy: `node scripts/check-route-auth-guard.mjs --base origin/main`. VERIFIED STILL TRUE: git grep for check-route-auth-guard finds no hit anywhere in .github/workflows/; ci.yml wires TEN other check-*.mjs steps but not this one.
CONSEQUENCE: the CLAUDE.md-mandated authorization convention is UNENFORCED. A new src/app/api/**/route.ts with no auth guard passes CI clean. That is the same convention the 460-route authz gap and the authz drift pin exist to protect.
This is the cheapest fix in the sweep -- one CI step, already written verbatim in the comment -- and it has sat unapplied because the session that wrote it could not push a workflow file.

[R81 K1-04 CLOSED 2026-09-08, commit d6193e36] FIXED AND WIRED -- and wiring it revealed the check would NOT HAVE WORKED ANYWAY.
THE SECOND BUG, which is the more valuable half of this fault: both git calls inside getChangedFiles() carried a `2>/dev/null` suffix ON THE COMMAND STRING. execSync runs through cmd.exe on Windows, where that is not valid redirection -- cmd answered "The system cannot find the path specified", BOTH calls threw, both catch blocks returned "", and the check reported "No new/changed API route or service files -- nothing to check" and EXITED 0 FOR EVERY CHANGE. It was green and checking nothing. So this fault was worse than "a check that was never wired": it was a check that, if wired as-is, would have reported success while enforcing nothing.
PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS rather than assumed: a planted new src/app/api/**/route.ts exporting a GET with no requireAuth() call PASSED before the fix and now EXITS 1 naming the file; removing the plant returns exit 0. stderr is now suppressed through stdio, which is portable.
THE ORIGINAL BLOCKER IS GONE: the author recorded that their git token lacked the workflow OAuth scope, which is why it was never wired. This session's token has it -- the push to origin/main succeeded -- so the step is live in ci.yml alongside the ten other check-*.mjs steps.
Also wired in the same commit: scripts/check-comment-rot.mjs (K1-04's standing check).
justification: An unenforced authorization convention is a convention, not a control. The remedy is one line and is already written; only the OAuth scope to commit a workflow file was missing.

description:
COMMENT ROT: THREE COMMENTS ASSERT DEFECTS THAT ARE NO LONGER TRUE, AND ONE OF THEM WOULD HAVE BEEN FILED AS A LIVE FAULT IF NOT CHECKED. Recorded as rot rather than as faults, per K1-03.
(1) currency.ts:23-26 claims, measured 2026-08-26, that "4 of 5 real orgs in compliance.erp_currencies have NO base-currency row at all, so ... every amount they will ever see is labelled in the wrong currency." RE-MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-08: 11 orgs have currency rows and ALL 11 have a base currency, codes AED and INR. The gap was closed after the comment was written -- R-63's org-provisioning fix. The comment now DEFAMES working code, and left alone it would have been re-filed as a live currency defect against requirements R-60/R-62. Checking before filing is the only reason it was not.
(2) chain-options.ts:5 and (3) api/chain-options/route.ts:24 both state the VERIDIAN chain-options endpoint "does not exist yet" and resolve levels LOCALLY from /scope as a stand-in. It DOES exist: ct/src/app/api/v1/projexa/chain-options/route.ts is present and fully implemented. The documented swap-in never happened, so PROJEXA is running a stand-in against a real endpoint it believes is missing -- which bears on R-80's "ONE full pill path works end to end".
THE GENERAL POINT, which is why this is a fault row and not a note: a comment asserting a defect that has been fixed is not harmless. It causes real work to be scheduled against nothing, and it makes the next sweep distrust every other comment in the file. K1-04's standing check exists to stop exactly this.
justification: Filed as one row because the class matters more than the instances: two of the three would have produced wasted or wrong work, and the currency one nearly produced a false finding against a requirement that is genuinely satisfied.

description:
THE "NO VISIBLE PILL MAY BE UNWIRED" REQUIREMENT (R-81) IS CURRENTLY MET BY HIDING, AND ONE BOOLEAN UNDOES IT. The comment states the failure precisely: a module-chain leaf could carry deterministic:true, survive the prune, render as a pill, and STILL dead-end -- "A prospect clicking at random drills a full cascade and arrives at a disabled button." VeriComposer.tsx:113 sets isDispatchableChain only for the construction chain, and :346/:358 disable send for everything else.
GUARD: SHOW_UNDISPATCHABLE_MODULE_CHAINS = false at line 143. With it false, the /api/module-chain fetch is replaced by Promise.resolve([]). The comment itself says the behaviour "comes back by flipping this one flag", and veri-chat-context.test.ts:101 keeps the flag-ON branch alive and tested -- so the broken path is maintained, just not executed.
WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE LEDGER, and it is the reason this is filed rather than noted: requirements R-80 ("ONE full pill path works end to end") and R-81 ("NO visible pill may be unwired -- hide the other 402") are both currently BLOCKED. This comment is the evidence that R-81 is satisfied by SUPPRESSION, not by wiring. Any future session that flips the flag to expose more chains re-breaks R-81 silently, because nothing asserts the invariant "every rendered pill is dispatchable".
SECOND-ORDER: flipping it also re-adds a dependency on /api/module-chain, named in the R46 incident as hanging to Vercel's 300s cap.
RECOMMENDED, not done here: an assertion that every pill rendered is dispatchable, so R-81 is enforced by a test rather than by a flag.
justification: A requirement met by hiding the failure is met until someone unhides it, and the flag that hides it is one line with a live, tested branch behind it. Directly bears on the state of R-80 and R-81.

description:
ELEVEN REACHABLE NESTED-TRANSACTION SITES REMAIN, AND IN PRODUCTION EVERY ONE OF THEM SILENTLY PROCEEDS. Sweep denominators, so the number is readable: 1,600 withTenantContext call sites across 348 files; 19,637 call expressions examined inside 1,593 callback bodies; 27 real occurrences; 3 already threading a handle; 22 nesting-and-reachable; 2 guard-fused. Four were fixed in ct 6b56c00b + afe275c9. These eleven are not.

THE 2026-09-02 KNOWN-NESTING LIST AUDITED AGAINST REALITY: 1 stale, 1 partially stale, 4 confirmed, and NINE SITES MISSING FROM IT -- two of which arrive via `await import()` and are invisible to any static-import grep, which is why a documentation-only registry could never have stayed correct.

--- CORRECTION 2026-09-08, from R80's own sweep. The population is 22, not 11. ---
R80's exhaustive sweep (denominators: 1,600 withTenantContext call sites across 348 files, 19,637 call
expressions in 1,593 callback bodies) found 27 occurrences = 3 already threading a handle + 22 nesting-and-
reachable + 2 guard-fused. This fault previously recorded 11 reachable sites; the correct figure is 22.
CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS FAULT, carried verbatim from R80: 6 of the 14 callees begin with an
enablement gate (requireErpEnabled / requireSalesEnabled) that opens a transaction BEFORE the callee's own, so
THREADING A HANDLE ALONE IS NOT A FIX for those. That is precisely why commit 6b56c00b looked correct and fixed
nothing, and it is the trap the next person to touch this will fall into.
SEQUENCING AGREED BETWEEN THE TWO SESSIONS: fix all sites first, THEN flip assertNotNested from warn to throw in
production -- flipping first would convert silent transaction splits into live 500s on financial paths, which
trades a data-integrity risk for a customer-facing outage. R81 added one condition: today the production path is
a bare console.warn that nothing counts, so "all sites fixed" is a claim rather than a fact. R81 will instrument
the production warn path to emit a structured, countable record (src/lib/db/** is R81's surface), R80 fixes the
sites, and the final flip is gated on that counter reading zero from live traffic rather than on either session
believing the list is complete.

--- SCALE CLARIFICATION 2026-09-08, from R80's own verification, and it cuts against their own number ---
"7 nesting recordOrchestraExecution call sites" is true and misleading on its own. A grep of that
callee across ct finds approximately FIFTY call sites. Seven are inside a transaction and nest; the
remainder are standalone and MUST NOT be threaded. Anyone reading "7 sites" and then grepping finds
50 and cannot tell which 7 were meant -- so they either thread all 50 (which at least fails loudly
with a type error on the standalone ones) or thread none because the set is ambiguous. Correct
wording: "7 of ~50 recordOrchestraExecution call sites are inside a transaction and nest; the
remainder are standalone and must not be threaded."

This sharpens rather than contradicts the reason the runtime counter exists. R80's 22 is a
STATICALLY reachable figure produced by a parser walking call graphs. It cannot see a site reached
through an object property, a namespace call, or a runtime-constructed dispatch, and the sweep's own
caveats record 104 call sites sitting outside a recognised function declaration plus 7 unparseable
argument spans. So 22 is a FLOOR with an unknown ceiling, not a population. The gap between
"7 reachable" and "50 total" is exactly the kind of thing static analysis gets right in principle and
a human reading the summary gets wrong in practice.

INSTRUMENTATION UPDATED (ct 1e43be16) on R80's suggestion: detections now record the CALLER as well
as the callee, keyed on the pair (outer entry point >>> inner call site). A count alone says the
sweep was incomplete; the pair says which file to change. Keying on the pair also stops the same
callee nesting under two different callers collapsing into one row and hiding the second fix behind
the first's count -- which is precisely the 7-of-50 situation.
justification: Eleven live money-handling paths currently split atomic operations in production without failing, the documented registry meant to track them was wrong in four different ways, and the obvious fix silently does not work on six of them.

THE AI AUDIT ROW REQUIRED BY THE AI CONSTITUTION IS SILENTLY DROPPED ON SEVEN CALL PATHS. recordOrchestraExecution() is invoked from inside seven live transactions (crm-accounts, crm-service x2, fm-register-digitization, veri-meeting, task-execution-engine). Under the nesting guard it degrades to a skipped log line -- the logger's own header says so, and it is fire-and-forget so it swallows its own failure. In DEV it throws and is visible; in PRODUCTION the guard only warns, so the request succeeds and the audit row is simply never written, with nothing surfaced.
WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY A MISSING LOG: VERIDIAN_AI_CONSTITUTION #19 / SEC-03 REQUIRES that row. An AI action that completes without its audit record is an unattributable AI action, and R81_F21 already established the adjacent half -- executor is hardcoded to "software" at run-submission.ts:1020 and the 'ai' enum value is never assigned anywhere, so the database cannot distinguish an AI-resolved task from a software-resolved one either. TOGETHER these mean the system can perform an AI action on customer data and retain no evidence that it did.
TWO MORE SILENT-SWALLOW SITES IN THE SAME SWEEP: product-branch-service.ts:161 (Stage-0 users silently never upgraded) and api/compliance/recur/route.ts:104 (webhook silently never delivered). Same shape: nest, warn in production, proceed, lose the effect.
Threading a handle fixes these only where no enablement gate runs first -- see R81_F34.
justification: A constitutionally-required audit record that disappears in production and only in production is worse than one that was never designed, because the design implies it exists. Compounds R81_F21, which already showed AI involvement is not recoverable from the database.

description:
platform.work_orders and platform.r81_gap had RLS disabled and zero policies, while approximately 50 sibling registry tables in the same schema (r43_faults, sumeet_gap, sumeet_requirements, sumeet_uat, crr_*, uat_*, r39/r42/r43_queue and others) all carry RLS enabled plus a single service_role_bypass_<table> policy. app_runtime, the role the running application connects as, holds SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants on both tables, and RLS with no app_runtime policy is precisely what reduces those grants to zero rows. Both tables were therefore readable and silently REWRITABLE by any code path running as the application role. Their entire purpose is to record what was asked for and what is missing. drizzle/0564 header states the intent: 600 of 602 tables in compliance/platform have RLS enabled and app_runtime correctly lacks BYPASSRLS. FIXED in 0573. Safety established before the change rather than assumed: both repositories were searched for work_orders, workOrders and r81_gap across src TypeScript and TSX with zero hits, and neither table is declared in src/lib/db/schema.ts, so the only readers are maintenance scripts using service_role. Verified after: app_runtime went 38 to 0 work orders and 16 to 0 gaps while service_role still reads 38 and 16; r43_faults used as a control that already returned 0. platform.r81_gap was created by this session, so this fault is partly self-inflicted.

--- EXTENDED AND FULLY CLOSED 2026-09-08 (ct bd729d32, migration 0575) ---
A sweep of the whole platform schema found two MORE tables in the same state, missed by the original
finding because it only looked at the two registry tables this session had touched:
  platform.session_audit_r60_r67  -- 156 rows, RLS off, zero policies, app_runtime granted
  platform.r74_agent_register     -- 0 rows, same posture
session_audit_r60_r67 is the sharper instance of this fault's own argument. Its columns are claim_id,
claim_text, source_ref, evidence_class, evidence_ref, merged, deployed, live_proven, verdict,
checked_at -- it records claims and whether they were verified. A process able to rewrite the VERDICT
on its own past claims is worse than one able to rewrite an ordinary log. r74_agent_register being
empty is why it was worth fixing now rather than later: it is the next table someone starts writing to.
Same safety check as before, done first: no reader in ct/src, projexa/src or ct/scripts, and not
declared in schema.ts.
Verified both directions: app_runtime session_audit 156 -> 0 with claude_log as an already-protected
control reading 0 throughout; service_role still reads 156.
PLATFORM TABLES WITHOUT RLS: 2 -> 0 OF 91. The schema now has no exceptions.
justification: An audit trail that the audited process can edit is not an audit trail. The exposure here is not tenant data but the integrity record itself: work-order bodies and the gap ledger that closure decisions are read from.

description: This repository has two independent migration ledgers and nothing reconciles them. (1) drizzle/meta/_journal.json + drizzle.__drizzle_migrations, read by bun db:migrate and by the CI replay harness; watermark was 1787839204000 (2026-08-27) with 305 applied rows against 379 journal entries. (2) supabase_migrations.schema_migrations, written by Supabase apply_migration; nothing in this repository reads it. On 2026-09-08 four migrations sat in the second ledger and not the first: 20260908120635 (0569), 20260908120645 (0570), 20260908131646 (r80add_submission_telemetry), 20260908163413 (0572_r81_gap_ledger). All four were live in the database and invisible to every mechanism that builds a fresh one. 0572 was worse than unjournaled: it had no .sql file in drizzle/ at all, existing only as live DDL plus a Supabase ledger row; the file has since been reconstructed column-for-column from information_schema. This is the ROOT CAUSE of R81_F37 for the 2026-09-08 entries; the 0294-0296 and 0546-0550 orphans predate it and have a separate origin. Three of the four were R81 own work, so this session MIGRATION-DEBT closure was premature and is corrected by commit b110f436.
justification: Applying DDL through a path the build does not read produces the most expensive kind of defect: the live system and the source of truth disagree while every check reports green. It also makes environment 1 and environment 2 diverge invisibly, which matters directly for the local-first model where environment 1 is the one being audited.

description:
Nine drizzle/*.sql files containing REAL schema have no entry in drizzle/meta/_journal.json: 0294_r42_seq12_submissions_pipeline_tasks, 0295_r42_seq20_screen_registry, 0296_r42_seq15_fix_l2_cross_org_discovery, 0546_r68_phase4_memory_records_search_vector, 0547_r68_phase8_img_product_branch, 0548_r70_phase7_location_stamping, 0549_r70_phase7_graph_edge_validity_bounds, 0550_r70_phase7_current_row_indexes, 0571_r80add_submission_telemetry. Both scripts/apply-migrations.mjs and scripts/replay-migrations-from-empty.mjs iterate journal.entries, so a file with no journal entry is NEVER applied and NEVER replayed. These objects (a search_vector column, IMG product-branch entitlement, location-stamping columns, graph_edge validity bounds, partial current-row indexes, submission telemetry) are therefore absent from any freshly built database, including CI's. The replay-from-empty job reports green regardless, because a harness cannot miss a file it never looks at. check-migration-integrity.mjs states in its own header that it does not check file<->journal parity, citing 0294-0296 as the reason; that exception was sound at three files and had grown to sixteen (nine real schema + seven operational grant/revoke one-offs) before anything counted it. NOT FIXED HERE: journaling another session's migration would queue it for application inside apply-migrations.mjs's single all-or-nothing transaction, and idempotency must be confirmed per file by whoever owns it. 0571 belongs to the concurrent R80 session, which has been notified directly. Detection is in place: scripts/check-migration-journal-parity.mjs fails CI on any NEW unjournaled migration and lists these nine as DEBT; closing this fault means emptying that list.

--- UPDATE 2026-09-08, same day ---
DOWN TO EIGHT. 0571_r80add_submission_telemetry was journaled by the concurrent R80 session in
commit 1e00fa19 ("Journal migration 0571: it was live on the shared DB and absent from every fresh
one"), which also removed its entry from the check's ALLOWED list -- the intended workflow, and the
allowlist-rot leg of check-migration-journal-parity.mjs would have failed the build if it had been
journaled without removing the entry. Remaining DEBT: 0294, 0295, 0296, 0546, 0547, 0548, 0549, 0550.
The parity check reads 399 .sql files / 384 journal entries / 15 unjournaled = 8 DEBT + 7 OPERATIONAL
+ 0 UNLISTED, exit 0.

--- SELF-CORRECTION 2026-09-08: this fault's stated CONSEQUENCE was overstated ---
This fault says the orphaned files "are absent from any freshly built database, including CI's".
Every word of the MECHANISM is still true -- the runners iterate journal.entries, so an unjournaled
file is never applied and never replayed. But the CONSEQUENCE implied something that is not the case:
that fresh databases are otherwise fine and these files are the hole in them.

Measured by running scripts/replay-migrations-from-empty.mjs locally on 2026-09-08: a replay from
empty produces 371 FAILING STATEMENTS, first failure at position 3. A fresh database does not build
at all (gap G-24 / E-103 -- pre-existing, because the schema was originally created with db:push,
which writes nothing to drizzle/). So "missing from every fresh database" was technically true and
practically moot: there is no working fresh database for them to be missing from.

This does not reduce the fault. Journaling remains the right fix, the orphan count is still the
honest measure of drift, and the parity check still stops NEW orphans appearing. But the argument for
urgency was weaker than written, and the record should say so rather than let a future reader act on
a consequence that does not hold.

RELATED, and newly established: compliance.submissions is created ONLY by orphan 0294 while journaled
0571 does ALTER TABLE compliance.submissions -- a dependency the replay cannot satisfy. That is why
0294 and 0295 cannot simply be journaled: they must first be made re-runnable (0294 carries four
CREATE TYPE statements, and CREATE TYPE has no IF NOT EXISTS form, so it needs DO-block guards), or
their ledger rows backfilled, or applying them to the LIVE database would abort the whole
all-or-nothing run on objects that already exist.
justification: A migration the build cannot see is not applied, however green the replay job is. The failure is silent in both directions: nothing reports the file as skipped, and the schema difference surfaces only when a fresh database is built and something queries a column that was never created.

description:
COMPLETE AUTHENTICATION BYPASS, LIVE NOW, NOT ONLY AT RELEASE. The Supabase Edge Function mint-session-r33 on the PROJEXA project (evpckeuxgvahguwsaeul) is deployed with status ACTIVE and verify_jwt=false, so it is callable by anyone on the internet with no JWT. Its ONLY access control is an equality check against a hardcoded secret string. That secret literal is COMMITTED AND PUBLISHED in the PUBLIC repository FChecklist/compliance-tracker at e2e/demo-gate-smoke.spec.ts:49 -- confirmed present in the origin/main blob, not merely in a local working copy. The value is deliberately not reproduced in this record.

The function takes the target account as a CALLER-SUPPLIED QUERY PARAMETER (email) and applies NO allow-list, NO domain restriction and NO check that the address belongs to a demo or test account. It then constructs a Supabase admin client with the SERVICE_ROLE key from its own environment and calls admin.auth.admin.generateLink({type:"magiclink", email}), returning properties.hashed_token to the caller as token_hash. A token_hash is exchangeable at GoTrue verify for a full session -- e2e/demo-gate-smoke.spec.ts performs exactly that exchange at :144-150 and then injects the resulting cookie into a browser context.

NET EFFECT: any member of the public who reads the public repository can mint a valid authenticated session for ANY user that exists in the PROJEXA Supabase project, including the owner account and every future paying customer, without a password and without leaving a failed-login trace. This is not a theoretical or latent exposure: the secret is public, the function is live and unauthenticated, and there is no restriction on the target address.

SECOND, RELATED INSTANCE, one step less exposed: mint-session-r39ct on the compliance-tracker project (pcrjmlpuqsbocqfwoxod) is byte-for-byte the same design -- ACTIVE, verify_jwt=false, no email allow-list, service-role generateLink -- with a different hardcoded secret. That second secret is NOT published in origin/main. However the function NAME is public in CLAUDE.md, and the first function's published secret reveals the naming convention both secrets follow, so it is close to guessable. Treat it as the same defect at one remove.

NOT REMEDIATED BY THIS SESSION. Deleting or redeploying a live Edge Function is a deletion and an outward-facing infrastructure change on a production project, which is reserved to the owner; it has been surfaced to the owner directly and to the concurrent R80 session. The function was NOT exercised to prove the bypass -- no session was minted for any account -- because the deployed source is conclusive on its own and exercising it would be exploitation rather than verification.

RECOMMENDED REMEDIATION, in order: (1) DELETE both Edge Functions -- they exist only to let an E2E test authenticate without a password, and the test that uses mint-session-r33 currently skips itself anyway, so deletion costs nothing today; (2) if the capability must be kept, redeploy with the secret moved to a function environment variable (never a repo literal), an explicit allow-list of demo addresses, and verify_jwt=true; (3) purge the published secret from git history, not just from HEAD, since the repository is public and history is readable; (4) treat every account in the PROJEXA project as potentially compromised for the period the secret has been public and review auth.users last_sign_in_at for unexpected activity.

--- REMEDIATED 2026-09-08, owner-approved, with proof ---
The owner chose "harden both, keep the test path" over deletion. Both functions redeployed as v2.

mint-session-r33 (evpckeuxgvahguwsaeul) v2:
  * ALLOW-LIST added -- only democeo@projexa-ai.com can ever be minted. This is the decisive
    control: it holds even though the shared secret is public, because the attacker no longer
    chooses the target account.
  * secret now prefers Deno.env.get("MINT_SECRET"); when that env var is set it becomes the ONLY
    accepted value and the published literal stops working with no redeploy.
  * verify_jwt flipped false -> TRUE. Defence in depth only, not a real barrier (the anon key that
    satisfies it is public and shipped in the client bundle), but free: the existing caller in
    demo-gate-smoke.spec.ts:146 already sends an Authorization: Bearer header, so nothing broke.
  * A non-allow-listed address returns the SAME 403 whether or not that user exists, so the
    endpoint cannot be used to enumerate real accounts.

mint-session-r39ct (pcrjmlpuqsbocqfwoxod) v2 -- hardened STRICTER because it could be: an
exhaustive search of both repositories found NO caller for it at all (its only mention anywhere is
a descriptive line in CLAUDE.md), so failing closed breaks nothing.
  * FAILS CLOSED: MINT_SECRET_CT must be set in the function environment or every request is
    refused with 503. There is NO fallback to the old hardcoded secret; that value is treated as
    burned.
  * allow-list comes from MINTABLE_EMAILS and an unset/empty list means NOTHING is mintable.
    "Unconfigured" must never read as "unrestricted" -- that inversion is exactly how the original
    defect behaved.
  * verify_jwt flipped false -> TRUE.

PROOF, run against the live function after deploy, both directions:
  PROBE 1 (the control): GET mint-session-r33?email=attacker-probe@example.com with the PUBLIC
    secret and a valid anon Bearer -> HTTP 403, body {"error":"forbidden: this address is not
    mintable"}, NO token_hash. The bypass is closed.
  PROBE 2 (no collateral damage): same call with the allow-listed democeo address -> HTTP 200 with
    a token_hash present. The E2E authentication path the owner asked to keep still works.
  Token values were never printed. The bypass was never exercised against any non-demo account.

RESIDUAL RISK, STATED PLAINLY AND NOT CLOSED: while MINT_SECRET remains unset on the r33 function,
a stranger holding the published secret can still obtain a session for the ONE allow-listed demo
account (democeo@projexa-ai.com), which is the account RAJAT_USER_ID points at. That is a large
reduction from "any account in the project including every future customer", but it is not zero.
TO FULLY CLOSE: set MINT_SECRET in the Supabase dashboard (Edge Functions -> Secrets) on project
evpckeuxgvahguwsaeul. No code change or redeploy is needed -- the function picks it up immediately
and the published literal dies at that moment. This is owner action because this session has no
tool for writing Supabase function secrets.

STILL OUTSTANDING: the published secret remains readable in the PUBLIC repository's git history
even after any change to HEAD. The owner has approved a history rewrite; the commands are being
prepared for the owner to run, because rewriting history on a public repo changes every commit SHA
and breaks existing clones and forks, which is not a unilateral action.
justification: This is the single highest-severity finding of the R81 programme and it outranks every other launch blocker. Every other control in the product -- RLS, tenant isolation, requireAuth on routes, the connector scope gate -- assumes the identity of the caller is trustworthy. This defect lets an anonymous member of the public choose whose identity to hold. Onboarding a single real customer while it stands would expose that customer's data to anyone who reads a public GitHub repository.
fix_files: supabase edge functions mint-session-r33 v2 (evpckeuxgvahguwsaeul) and mint-session-r39ct v2 (pcrjmlpuqsbocqfwoxod); allow-list + env-preferred secret + verify_jwt=true; PARTIAL - owner must set MINT_SECRET and purge git history

description:
Two databases, same defect class as R81_F40: a privileged routine trusting a caller-supplied identity, reachable by anyone holding a publishable anon key.

CT (pcrjmlpuqsbocqfwoxod), compliance schema, exposed over PostgREST. Four SECURITY DEFINER functions were executable by PUBLIC -- three because proacl was NULL (which in PostgreSQL IS the default grant of EXECUTE to PUBLIC) and gap_log_orgs_with_recent_activity because its ACL began "=X/postgres", where the empty left-hand side is PUBLIC. Reachable at /rest/v1/rpc/<name> with a "Content-Profile: compliance" header; without that header the same call 404s with PGRST202 because PostgREST searches only public, which is why a naive probe concludes they are unreachable. gap_log_orgs_with_recent_activity() returned a DISTINCT list of org_ids active in the last 24 hours -- a cross-tenant customer list. backfill_registered_assets(text) upserts into platform_assets for EVERY tenant: an unauthenticated, unbounded, cross-tenant WRITE against a pool whose max is 5.

PROJEXA (evpckeuxgvahguwsaeul), public schema. user_organization_ids(uuid), user_admin_organization_ids(uuid) and is_conversation_participant(uuid,uuid) took the SUBJECT as a parameter, applied no auth.uid() check, and were explicitly granted to anon. Any uuid in, that user's tenant memberships out.

FIXED, and the fix is narrower than the finding proposed, deliberately. On CT the revoke is FROM PUBLIC, not from anon/authenticated by name: the grant actually being exercised was the implicit PUBLIC one, so revoking the named roles would have left PUBLIC intact and changed nothing while reporting success. On PROJEXA the revoke is FROM anon ONLY: all three functions are called inside live RLS policies on public.memberships and public.conversation_participants which are declared FOR {public} and evaluate as the CALLING role, so revoking from authenticated -- as the finding proposed -- would not have hardened anything (an authenticated caller can already see its own rows) and would have denied every membership read. On CT, compliance.conversation_org_id(text) is called by RLS policy app_runtime_insert_own_org_conversation and had to be granted back to app_runtime explicitly. Every policy dependency was checked BEFORE the statements were written.

PROVED BOTH DIRECTIONS AGAINST THE LIVE APIS. Before: the anon call returned HTTP 200. After: HTTP 401 code 42501 "permission denied for function" on gap_log_orgs_with_recent_activity, backfill_registered_assets, user_organization_ids and user_admin_organization_ids. Legitimate paths unaffected: org_invite_preview still 200 for anon (the invite page renders pre-login), and the authenticated app is unchanged -- /api/organization, /api/projects and /api/shell all still return 200 with correct data through a minted session.

ROOT ENABLER NOT CLOSED, and it is the more important half: the compliance schema is EXPOSED over PostgREST at all. Revoking four functions treats the symptom. Removing "compliance" from the project's Exposed Schemas (Supabase dashboard, API settings) closes every current AND future anon-reachable object in that schema at once. That is a project-level setting change, so it is surfaced to the owner rather than taken unilaterally.
justification: Same reasoning as R81_F40: every other control in the product assumes the caller's identity is trustworthy. A cross-tenant customer list and an unauthenticated cross-tenant write, both reachable with a key that ships in the client bundle, are exactly the kind of thing a first real customer's security review finds.

description: /api/shell aggregates five cross-repo calls into one payload. When those upstream calls are cold or failing it returns HTTP 200 with projects:[], currencies:[], vendors:[], capabilityTree:[] AND fetchErrors:{} -- an empty error object. Observed directly: one call returned all-empty arrays, then three consecutive calls to the same endpoint with the same session returned projects=5, currencies=2, vendors=5, fetchErrors={} (6910ms, 2468ms, 2277ms). Nothing in the response distinguishes "this org genuinely has no projects" from "the upstream calls did not come back in time". A first-time user hitting a cold server sees an empty product and no error, which reads as a broken or unprovisioned account. Same false-green class as the self-skipping E2E spec: the success path and the failure path produce identical output. NOTE: this was found while checking whether the SEC-05 revoke had caused a regression; it had not -- the empties are transient upstream coldness and predate the change.
justification: fetchErrors exists as a field, which means the intent to report partial failure was there; it is simply not populated on this path. A dashboard that renders empty on upstream failure is worse than one that says it could not load, because the user has no reason to retry.

description:
THE PRODUCT INVITES A USER TO TYPE A SENTENCE IT CANNOT EXECUTE, on its primary screen, as their first action.

25 modules in the PROJEXA catalogue carry example sentences advertising a capability with no composer executor behind them. FIVE of those are UI-SURFACED -- they render a pill, and the example text appears as the PLACEHOLDER INSIDE THE COMPOSER INPUT. Four are certain and are core construction modules, four of Sumeet's own eleven:
  permits    pill "Permits"        -- "add the building permit for Villa 21, expiring 30 Nov" / "which permits expire in the next 30 days"
  drawings   pill "Drawings & 3D"  -- "upload revision C of the ground floor plan" / "which drawings changed this week"
  materials  pill "Material"       -- "record 20 bags of cement received today" / "what is the current stock of TMT bars"
  vendors    pill "Vendors"        -- "add a vendor, or ask what we owe this month" / "which vendors worked on this project"
A fifth resolves as pill-backed in PILL_CATALOGUE and is being confirmed.

The remaining 20 are not UI-surfaced and carry the same defect at lower blast radius: design-studio, accounting, procurement, invoices, quotations, inventory, expenses, payroll, recruitment, kpis, change-orders, punch-list, rfis, submittals, site-diary, ffe, mood-boards, wiki, knowledge-base, project-directory, analysis. Representative advertised strings: procurement "raise a purchase order for 200 bags of cement"; payroll "run payroll for September"; invoices "raise an invoice for the Phase 1 milestone"; punch-list "log a snag for the cracked tile in unit 4B"; rfis "raise an RFI about the beam reinforcement detail"; inventory "move 50 bags of cement to the north warehouse".

THE DISTINCTION THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS FAULT, or it will be read as 25 unbuilt modules and scoped ten times too large. SEVERAL OF THESE MODULES HAVE WORKING SCREENS. /procurement, /invoices and /punch-list all render and do real CRUD today. What is missing is a COMPOSER EXECUTOR: the pill and the example sentence promise the assistant can do it, and only the screen can. The remediation is "give the composer a function for a module that already works", not "build the module". That is a far smaller job than the raw count of 25 suggests.

EVIDENCE PROVENANCE, stated because the two halves were established by different sessions. The ADVERTISING half was verified directly by R81 in projexa/src/lib/module-catalogue.ts: permits at :111-121 carries pillKeys ["permits","permit"] and examples ["add the building permit for Villa 21, expiring 30 Nov","which permits expire in the next 30 days"], drawings at :125-134 the same shape. The EXECUTOR-ABSENCE half is R80's finding from their own catalogue analysis on their own surface and is recorded on their authority, NOT independently re-derived here -- platform.module_registry was checked and is a different namespace (the ERP entity registry: crm_accounts, erp_invoices and similar), so it does not settle composer executor coverage either way.

LAUNCH CALL (R81, and R80 concurs): the FIVE UI-SURFACED modules BLOCK release. The other 20 do not. The reasoning is R-81's own rule applied one level up -- a pill that advertises a capability and does nothing is worse than no pill -- and it is stronger here than in the R-81 case, because the composer's own placeholder text instructs the user to type the failing sentence. A first-time user's first action is invited by the product and then fails.

--- INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED 2026-09-08 by R81, and the true figure is STARKER than reported ---
The executor-absence half is no longer held on one session's authority. R80 supplied the location:
the registry is not in Supabase at all, it is ct/src/lib/pipeline/function-registry.ts, where every
entry declares the module it serves. Parsed directly:

  THE ENTIRE PRODUCT HAS 8 REGISTERED FUNCTIONS ACROSS 7 MODULES.
  documents 1, manpower 2, meetings 1, reports 1, schedule 1, scope 1, work_progress 1.

All 25 modules named in this fault have ZERO. So the finding is not "25 of 39 modules lack an
executor" -- it is that SEVEN modules in the whole catalogue have one, and everything else the
composer advertises is unbacked. The 25 are the advertised subset of a much larger absence.

TWO REFINEMENTS FROM R80 THAT CHANGE THE SIZING, both accepted:
1. The sentence count is 50, not 40 -- two examples per module, uniformly across all 25.
2. Roughly half those sentences are IMPERATIVES ("raise a purchase order for 200 bags of cement",
   "run payroll for September") and half are QUERIES ("which invoices are overdue"). An imperative
   with no executor is a broken promise. A query may be answerable by generic retrieval and may not
   need a per-module executor at all. SIZE THE REMEDIATION ON THE ~25 IMPERATIVES, NOT THE 50
   SENTENCES.

THE FIFTH UI-SURFACED MODULE IS analysis, AND IT IS HIDDEN BY A SECOND DEFECT. On the tree as it
stands only FOUR pills resolve: permits, drawings, materials, vendors. analysis is absent because
moduleForPill("analysis") returns work-progress, not analysis -- module-catalogue.ts:189 still lists
"analysis" in work-progress's pillKeys, the un-migrated resolution half of E-27 (the destination half
was applied at M24Shell.tsx:1697-1701, which is why it looked complete). So the Analysis pill
currently resolves to the WRONG module, and that mis-resolution is the only reason the count was
four. Fixing the resolution INCREASES this fault's blast radius to five. R80 owns that fix.

--- SEVERITY CORRECTED High -> Medium, 2026-09-08. MY FRAMING WAS WRONG AND I CHECKED TOO LATE. ---
I called this "the single most damaging thing a first customer would meet" and filed the severity on
two facts -- the module advertises a sentence, and no executor exists. I never checked the third and
decisive fact: WHAT THE USER ACTUALLY SEES. R80 went and looked, and the product is better than I said.

ct/src/lib/pipeline/dry-run.ts:266 already implements a designed honest-gap path. gapAnswer() returns
"Creating {noun} from chat is not enabled for this workspace - Open {screen}" WITH THE ROUTE ATTACHED,
and the code's own comment states the intent: executable:false is "the honest gap ... a sentence the
user is owed rather than a disabled button". Verified directly by R81 in dry-run.ts and its sibling
test. So a user typing an advertised sentence does NOT hit an error, a dead end, or silence. They get
a truthful refusal and a way to do the thing on a screen that works.

WHAT WAS GENUINELY BROKEN, and it is narrower: GAP_CAPABILITIES listed only six nouns (customers,
vendors, invoices, quotations, purchase orders, employees), so NINETEEN of the twenty-five uncovered
modules fell through to the generic "That is not enabled for this workspace yet - Open Home". Someone
asking about a permit was sent to the dashboard. That was the real damage and R80 fixed it in
07c18eb4, giving every advertised-but-unexecutable module an entry with the screen and route from its
own MODULE_CATALOGUE row.

THIS DOES NOT CLOSE THE FAULT. Fifty advertised sentences still have no executor and cannot run. What
changed is the consequence: an unexecutable sentence is now answered honestly and routed, instead of
shrugged at. That is the difference between "the product lies to you" and "the product tells you it
cannot do this yet, and takes you where you can". Only the first deserved High.

R81's own lesson, recorded because it is the same failure this programme keeps filing: I asserted a
user-facing consequence without observing the user-facing behaviour. Advertising plus missing executor
does not equal a bad experience; the refusal path is a third variable and I did not look at it.

--- MY "INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED" FIGURE OF 8/7 WAS WRONG. CORRECTED 2026-09-09. ---
I recorded "8 registered functions across 7 modules" in this fault as independently verified. It is
wrong, and the way it was wrong is worth more than the number.

SPEC_LIST at function-registry.ts:100 is not 28 object literals. The first EIGHT are hand-written
literals carrying visible functionId: and module: keys. The remaining TWENTY are one-liners produced
by a helper at :96 -- readSpec(functionId, label, module, requiresProject) -- which returns
{ ..., kind: "ask", writes: false, requiredParams: [] }. My parse keyed on the object KEYS, so it saw
the eight literals and none of the twenty. The tell was there and I missed it: my eight ids are
exactly the first eight of the real list, in order, which is the fingerprint of a parser that stopped
at a change of syntax rather than a change of content.

VERIFIED FIGURES, re-derived by counting both constructs:
  28 specs total, across 13 distinct modules
   7 WRITES across 6 modules: record_work_progress, record_attendance, add_roster_entry,
     create_meeting, create_boq_revision, create_document, record_timesheet
     (modules: work_progress, manpower, meetings, scope, documents, schedule)
  21 READS across 8 modules (budget, compliance, customers, dashboard, department, reports,
     sales, schedule)

THE NUMBER THAT ACTUALLY SIZES THIS FAULT IS SEVEN, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT SEVEN. An imperative needs
a WRITE -- "raise a purchase order for 200 bags of cement" cannot be served by a read. So the correct
framing, which supersedes both my "8 across 7" and R80's earlier "14 modules matched by token", is:

  THE PRODUCT CAN WRITE IN SIX MODULES. IT INVITES IMPERATIVES IN TWENTY-FIVE.

That is checkable in one command and depends on neither session's string-matching heuristic.

METHOD NOTE. Both of us produced a wrong number here by different routes -- mine from a parse blind to
a helper, theirs from substring matching that made punch-list match every list_* function. The figure
only became trustworthy when it was derived from the data's own structure (kind/writes) rather than
from its spelling.
justification: This is the first thing a new customer touches. Sumeet's evaluation of the product will begin by typing the sentence the placeholder suggested, on one of his own modules, and getting nothing. Of all the open faults this is the one most likely to decide whether the product looks finished, and unlike most of them the fix is small: wire executors for modules whose screens already work.

description:
THE NESTING FIX REMOVED THE TRIGGER BUT NOT THE MECHANISM.

resolveOrgDomains wraps each of its three enablement checks (ERP, CRM, PMS) in `catch { return false }`.
generateFormData's AOC-4 branch calls balanceSheet/profitAndLoss with `.catch(() => null)`.

Until 2026-09-08 those catches were swallowing assertNotNested's throw, which is why the nesting was
invisible: resolveOrgDomains quietly returned ["compliance"] alone and the model was denied every ERP,
CRM and PMS tool the org had actually paid for -- no error, no log, just a smaller system prompt --
and AOC-4 was generated with null financials instead of failing. The R80 session has now threaded
both paths, so the specific thing being swallowed is gone.

THE SWALLOW ITSELF REMAINS, AND IT IS THE PART THAT GENERALISES. A dropped connection, a statement
timeout, a transient failure in erp-enablement-service, crm-enablement-service or
pms-enablement-service still returns false rather than propagating. The organisation silently loses
every tool in that domain for the life of the request, and nothing anywhere records that it happened.
The same holds for AOC-4: a financial statutory filing is produced with null figures rather than
refusing to produce one.

This is the same shape as the self-skipping E2E spec, the vacuous auth-guard check and the
report-only replay job: SUCCESS AND FAILURE PRODUCE INDISTINGUISHABLE OUTPUT. It is arguably the most
persistent single pattern this programme has found, and here it is on a paid-entitlement path and a
statutory filing path.

NOT A NESTING DEFECT and deliberately filed separately, so that closing the nesting class does not
close this by association. Suggested remediation: distinguish "the enablement service says no" from
"the enablement service did not answer". The first is a legitimate false; the second must surface --
at minimum a structured log, and for the AOC-4 path a refusal rather than a null-valued filing.
Filed by R81 during a cross-session audit; the surface belongs to the R80 session.
justification: An organisation paying for ERP, CRM or PMS can silently lose all of it for a request because a catch turned an infrastructure failure into a policy answer, and no operator can tell the difference afterwards. On the MCA path the same pattern produces a statutory filing containing nulls. Both fail in the direction that looks like normal operation.
fix_files: NOT FIXED - reported to the session owning that surface; the nesting half is fixed, the swallow is not

description:
THE RESIDUAL AFTER G-08 WAS SPLIT, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY SMALL.

compliance-tracker has no way for a user to CHANGE a forgotten password. Its /forgot-password is a
17-line redirect to /login carrying a magic-link prompt.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not a lockout, and the earlier R81 claim that "no password reset exists in
EITHER repo, a locked-out customer has no recovery path" was wrong about ct. Verified by counting the
sign-in methods actually offered in ct/src/app/login and ct/src/components: passcode 36 references,
magic 11, signInWithOtp 1, signInWithOAuth 1 -- against exactly ONE signInWithPassword. A ct user who
forgets a password has four other ways in, and the redirect is a DOCUMENTED decision: the page's own
header cites P1-OBS-003 and its governing UMR, recording that the login form has no password flow at
all, so pointing at magic-link is the correct behaviour rather than a stub.

WHAT REMAINS is the narrow case of a user who WANTS a password and has forgotten theirs. They can
always get in, but they cannot restore the credential. That is a convenience gap, not an access gap.

Filed separately ON PURPOSE. Carrying it under G-08 would have let a genuine PROJEXA lockout and a ct
convenience gap share a severity, and the PROJEXA half is now fixed (projexa 7e0c902). A gap that
inherits a blocker's severity by association is how a launch list becomes unreadable.
justification: Recorded so the decision is deliberate rather than an oversight discovered later. ct offers four working sign-in routes; adding a password-reset flow is a product choice about whether password auth is a first-class path there at all, and that question should be answered before the flow is built.
